title: across-refs reports a genuine id collision as one task with disagreeing states
description:
Found while building the Quest board mod (QCLI-431), whose pane creates tasks.

quest task create takes the next id from the working tree plus every LOCAL ref (QCLI-279/290), so a record that is written but not yet committed in ANOTHER checkout of the same repository is invisible to it. Reproduced during QCLI-431 with two worktrees of one repository: a create on main left uncommitted, then a create on feat/other, and both minted T-1. Committing the first closed the window and the next create minted T-2. ODOC-379 was minted this way on 2026-10-02 -- the operator test record from the prototype New task box, created in opum-doc checkout while a branch held the same id, and the fleet sweep tracker read failed on it.

The allocator half cannot be closed from inside the process: it cannot see another worktree uncommitted files, and it deliberately never fetches. Detection can be closed, and is not.

quest task list --across-refs treats the same id on two refs as two STATES of one task and picks no winner. That is right for the shape it was built for -- one task whose status differs across refs -- and silently wrong for a genuine collision, where two distinct records share an id. The read then reports a single task whose states disagree, and the fact that there are two different records never surfaces.

QCLI-431 carries the pane-side half only: the board draws an unlanded record as the collision window it is, so the person can land it. Detection belongs here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task list --across-refs distinguishes a genuine collision -- the same id on two refs naming records that are not the same task -- from one task whose states disagree across refs, and reports the former rather than folding it into the latter.

The discriminator it uses is stated in the record and is defensible from the data a task record actually carries; a pair it cannot tell apart is reported as an unresolved collision rather than assumed to be one task.

A test reproduces the QCLI-431 shape -- two refs carrying the same id for two different tasks -- and asserts the collision is reported, alongside a test that the legitimate same-task-different-states read is unchanged.
The behaviour is recorded in the --across-refs guide and in the task-creation guide section on refs-aware allocation.

plan: Discriminator: compare createdAt across the states of a same-id group (createdAt is per-record and survives refs; two independent creates do not share it); choose createdAat over title so a title edit on a PR head is not misread as a collision

Add an additive per-entry identity field (task | collision | unresolved) to the across-refs entry; a missing createdAt on any state is unresolved, never assumed one task; keep conflict and every existing field unchanged
Tests: reproduce the QCLI-431 shape (two refs, same id, two different createdAt) asserting the collision is reported; assert the legitimate same-task-different-status read is unchanged
Document in the --across-refs guide and the task-creation guide refs-aware allocation section; run bun run check
implementationNotes:
QCLI-432 AC2. THE DISCRIMINATOR, and why it is defensible from what a task record actually carries.

A same-id group is ONE TASK iff every state carries the SAME createdAt. createdAt is used rather than the title because a task's title can be edited on a PR head -- an edit would read as a collision under a title comparison -- while createdAt is written once at create and read back verbatim from every ref that carries the record, so it survives ref changes that move title or status. Two independent creates that minted the same id (the QCLI-431 shape) do not share a creation stamp.

createdAt is OPTIONAL on a task record, so a state carrying none cannot be compared: that group is `unresolved`, reported as a collision rather than assumed to be one task (AC2's second clause).

OUTPUT: an additive per-entry `identity: "task" | "collision" | "unresolved"`. `conflict` (status divergence within one task) is unchanged, every existing field stays, and no top-level envelope key moves -- the addition is inside each entry under `data`.

TESTS (AC3): the QCLI-431 collision shape is reproduced in the QCLI-417 fixture (a ref carrying T-1 as a DIFFERENT record, different createdAt and title) and asserted `collision`; the legitimate same-task-different-status read is asserted `task`; and a record with no createdAt is asserted `unresolved`. The existing suite (38 tests) stays green.

DOCS (AC4): the `task list --across-refs` help and the task-creation guide's refs-aware allocation section both describe `identity` and the collision window.
finalSummary: QCLI-432 made task list --across-refs distinguish a genuine id collision from one task whose states disagree across refs. Each entry now carries an additive identity: task (every state shares one createdAt), collision (two or more distinct createdAt values, i.e. different records sharing an id), or unresolved (two or more states that cannot be compared because one carries no createdAt; a lone state is always task). The discriminator is createdAt, chosen over title so a PR-head title edit is not misread as a collision; it is stated and defended in the task note, the code docblock and both guides (AC2). Tests reproduce the QCLI-431 collision shape, the legitimate status-conflict read, the unresolved pair and the lone case (AC3). Delivered in PR #557 (head aeab619a), reviewed over two rounds plus a DEC-172 (4ab) confirmatory check (reviews seq 7975, 7976, 7991), landed to dev as 972b55d0. The identity shape is PROVISIONAL pending opum-doc.
